name: High-grade Neuroendocrine Carcinoma of the Corpus Uteri
aliases: High-grade neuroendocrine carcinoma of the endometrium

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of Female Reproductive Organs

criteria.description: Histological confirmation of high-grade neuroendocrine carcinoma with small cell or large cell morphology
Positive immunohistochemical staining for neuroendocrine markers such as synaptophysin, chromogranin A, and CD56
Exclusion of primary neuroendocrine carcinoma from other anatomical sites
Presentation with abnormal uterine bleeding or pelvic mass

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation with positive neuroendocrine immunohistochemical markers and exclusion of other primary sites
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of histology, immunohistochemistry, and clinical correlation.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Pelvic mass detected on physical examination

searchTerms: pain in lower belly or pelvis
fatigue related to low red blood cells

occasional.symptomName: Lower extremity edema due to lymphatic obstruction
searchTerms: lower limb edema due to lymphatic obstruction
difficulty passing stool due to pelvic growth

rare.symptomName: Neurological symptoms due to paraneoplastic syndromes
searchTerms: nerve symptoms from cancer-related immune effects
neurological signs due to paraneoplastic syndrome
nerve problems linked to cancer immune response

laboratory: Possible elevated ACTH in paraneoplastic Cushing syndrome
imaging: MRI pelvis demonstrating invasive tumor with possible lymph node involvement
genetic: No specific germline mutations identified; somatic mutations may include TP53 and RB1 alterations
other: Histopathology showing small or large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma morphology
Immunohistochemical positivity for synaptophysin, chromogranin A, and CD56

distinguishingFeatures: Typically lower grade and less aggressive
Biphasic tumor with both carcinomatous and sarcomatous components
Different clinical behavior and treatment approach

redFlags: Evidence of distant metastases at diagnosis
references: WHO Classification of Tumors of Female Reproductive Organs, 5th Edition, 2020
Orphanet: High-grade neuroendocrine carcinoma of the corpus uteri (ORPHA:213731)
